With Apple reportedly planning to unveil new products on October 13, here's when the company could announce the date of its event based on its history of October events.

Will Apple hold an October event?

While the history of Apple's September events tends to follow a fairly regular pattern, the history of its October events is less precise, both in terms of when they are held and how far in advance they are announced.

Since 2010, Apple has held only 10 October events, the most recent being the Halloween-themed "Scary Fast" event on the evening of October 30, 2023.

Here's how far in advance Apple has announced each of its October events since 2010:

Year Event Announcement date Event date 2023 “Scary Fast” Tuesday, October 24 Monday, October 30 2021 “Unleashed” Tuesday, October 12 Monday, October 18 2020 “Hi, Speed” Tuesday, October 6 Tuesday, October 13 2018 “There’s more in the making” Thursday, October 18 Tuesday, October 30 2016 “Hello again” Wednesday, October 19 Thursday, October 27 2014 “It’s been way too long” Wednesday, October 8 Thursday, October 16 2013 “We still have a lot to cover” Tuesday, October 15 Tuesday, October 22 2012 “We’ve got a little more to show you” Tuesday, October 16 Tuesday, October 23 2011 “Let’s talk iPhone” Tuesday, September 27 Tuesday, October 4 2010 “Back to the Mac” Wednesday, October 13 Wednesday, October 20

That said, Bloomberg recently reported that Apple is planning to release the long-rumored smart home hub, a new-generation HomePod mini, and an Apple TV 4K with all-new Siri AI features on October 13 (Tuesday), but did not say whether the company would hold an event to unveil these products.

If so, Apple could announce the event date as early as next Monday (October 5), but no later than October 7 (Wednesday).

It's worth noting that Apple is also expected to announce an iPad mini with an OLED display, a new iMac, and several new MacBook Pro models (including one with a touchscreen) in 2026. Therefore, it remains to be seen whether these products will be unveiled at the same event, at another separate event, or via press release.

Looking back, Apple unveiled new Macs over three consecutive days via press releases in October 2024, while in October 2025, it announced the M5 chip and new iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, and Apple Vision Pro models without holding an event.

By contrast, Apple has held only one event in November, back in 2020, when its "One More Thing" event unveiled the first Macs powered by the M1 Apple silicon chip.

Of course, 2020 was an unusual year for Apple's announcement schedule — the company held an unusual WWDC at the end of June, followed by separate events in September and October, as the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted its usual timeline.

What new products do you think Apple will announce at its rumored October event? Let us know in the comments.
